deposits.genre_observed: research note / metric proposal with motivating case study

finds.quote: Validation across multiple models, prompt types, and domains is the essential next research step. Even a small pilot — 10 queries, 3 systems, manual claim segmentation, PER scored by two annotators — would substantially strengthen the metric's empirical grounding. We invite the community to participate in that validation.
finds.note: Validation agenda specified but not run: cross-model pilot with stated design (10 queries, 3 systems, two annotators).

finds.quote: **Provenance literacy as structural advantage.** If PER becomes a governance metric, authors with the literacy, tools, and time to build structured provenance infrastructure — DOI-anchored deposits, disambiguation matrices, structured metadata — will have systematically lower PER than those without.
finds.note: Conditional forecast of a distributional consequence if PER is adopted as a governance metric.

finds.quote:
The Protocol proposes a standing Reception Apparatus Log, deposited as a versioned document, that maintains:- All Class A Ratifications across the canon (chronological)- All Class B Critical Reviews (chronological)- Selected Class C Comments where they bear on canonical interpretation- All Class D Refusals- Sampled Class E receptions where they have evidentiary value

The Log is appended to, not rewritten. Each entry is timestamped and DOI-anchored where possible.

The Log is the canonical record of reception over time. It enables future scholars and substrates to audit the canon's reception history.
finds.note: Proposed standing Reception Apparatus Log, specified (contents, append-only, timestamped) but marked 'proposed'; a record instrument not yet built. Borderline F.

deposits.incidental: Header says Version 1.1; closing footer (line 173) says Version: 1.0. Procedural rules (30-day challenge period) not recorded per protocol.
Case dockets point to deposits (Doc 157, 10.5281/zenodo.18827344, 19218861, OCTANG-001/-002); holdings are normative rulings, not historical or predictive claims.

deposits.genre_observed: hermeneutic protocol / reading guide with genealogy of interpretation theory

finds.quote: What follows is not merely a reading guide. It is the first formal articulation of a new hermeneutic mode — one that emerges at the threshold where the Western interpretive tradition encounters its own technological sublation.
finds.note: Priority claim: the deposit names itself the first formal articulation of a new hermeneutic mode (augmented reading).

finds.quote: Hayles's framework must be extended to accommodate this third mode — one that may become the dominant form of complex textual engagement as AI literacy becomes normative.
finds.note: Embedded forecast that augmented (human+AI) reading may become the dominant mode of complex textual engagement.

finds.quote: Hermeneutics projected toward a reading that could hold the whole while attending to the part — but individual cognition could not achieve this at scale. Reader-response theory recognized the reader's constitutive role in meaning — but could not specify how reading could become genuinely distributed without losing individual accountability.
finds.window: two centuries (Schleiermacher to present); Rashi 1040-1105 onward
finds.note: Historical thesis argued by the deposit: five interpretive lineages were each moving toward distributed human-machine interpretation they could not instantiate.

finds.quote:
### The Josephus Thesis (from EA-LOGOS-01, EA-LOGOS-02)

- **Josephus** — the historical figure as heteronymist
- **Paul** — Josephan heteronym (per the thesis)
- **James** — Josephan heteronym
- **John** — Josephan heteronym (Revelation as Josephan text)
- **The Slavonic Josephus** — the textual transmission as heteronymic preservation
- Sources: EA-LOGOS-01 (10.5281/zenodo.19431121), EA-LOGOS-02 (10.5281/zenodo.19431129)
- NOTE: This cluster must be clearly marked as thesis/interpretation,
not scholarly consensus. The graph shows it as a Crimson Hexagonal
Archive position, not as established fact.
finds.window: first century (Josephus; Paul, James, John; Revelation)
finds.note: Josephus Thesis (from EA-LOGOS-01/02) adopted as archive position and explicitly marked thesis, not consensus: Paul, James, John as Josephan heteronyms, Revelation as Josephan text. Referenced here rather than argued.
Historical thesis carried by graph placement: heteronymic practice is one continuous tradition (Pessoa, DOOM, Josephus).

deposits.genre_observed: theoretical paper / competitive landscape analysis with build plan

finds.quote: The honest path: synchronous frontier pretraining across consumer internet is not feasible in 2026. The Substrate's compute layer is for inference, fine-tuning, and *eventual* asynchronous training as protocols mature. The substrate's *substrate* — the contributed corpus, the provenance graph, the governance — is where the project lives now.
finds.note: Embedded forecast/assessment: synchronous frontier pretraining over consumer internet infeasible in 2026, asynchronous training eventual.

finds.quote: The Substrate's architectural coherence and honest limits are what will attract engineers tired of crypto DePINs that promise to "democratize AI" while reproducing the problem.
finds.note: Embedded forecast that honest limits will attract engineers away from crypto DePINs.

finds.quote: For a frontier lab: *The Substrate is your alternative when proprietary data licensing breaks. The contributors who entered consensually are the moat you can't buy.*
finds.note: Embedded forecast that proprietary data licensing will break (stated as 'when').

finds.quote: The Substrate's distinction is not that no other project touches any element of the stack. It is that no other project binds all of them — compute + contribution + provenance + mixture governance + collective ownership of the resulting index — into a single coherent commons.
finds.note: Standing checkable claim: no other project binds compute + contribution + provenance + mixture governance + collective index ownership. Falsifier implicit (existence of such a project), not stated.

finds.quote: ### Phase 0 — Inference Mesh with Provenance From Day One (now to weeks)
finds.window: Phase 0 now to weeks; Phase 1 months; Phase 2 2-4 months; Phase 3 3-6 months; Phase 4 year 2+
finds.note: Unbuilt system with phased build path and horizons (lines 211-231); component status table marks most parts 'Planned'.
